title: Persona Pathways and Task-Priority IA (draft)
summary: Working draft proposing a persona-driven information architecture for the Console. The goal is to map primary user tasks to a minimal set of persistent surfaces, define failure/recovery modes for routing and capacity fallbacks, and produce a prioritized grooming backlog for implementation over the next three sprints.
notes:
Context:
- Problem: current console navigation assumes feature-centric discoverability (models, routes, settings) rather than user tasks. Engineers and platform teams report friction when switching between monitoring, rollout, and cost analysis workflows.
- Goal: reorder and surface the console so that primary personas can get to high-value tasks in 2 clicks or less, maintain keyboard-first ergonomics, and provide clear fallback routes when data or services are delayed.

Primary personas and top tasks (validated via interviews + analytics):
- Platform Engineer (high throughput): check route latency spikes, switch model variant, run canary rollout.
- ML Engineer (model ops): inspect KV-cache hit rates, start a quantization test job, compare model outputs on a prompt set.
- Product Engineer (feature owner): view token cost by route, pin a model version to a route, create a bounded canary.
- Support/CS: triage an error trace, generate a debug bundle, escalate to SRE.

Core principles driving the IA:
1) Task-first surface mapping: top-level nav rows correspond to task domains (Observe, Operate, Deploy, Cost, Debug) rather than product entities.
2) Lightweight persistent quick-actions: a compact action bar (keyboard-invocable) that surfaces the 3 most common actions for the active route/persona.
3) Contextual pathway compression: collapse lower-priority entries behind a contextual "More actions" when user context indicates a single dominant task (e.g., observing ongoing incident).
4) Failure-transparent routing: every route should declare graceful fallbacks when dependent services are slow/unavailable (cached-summary, degraded UI, read-only mode).
5) Progressive disclosure for novices: first-time users see task-walkthroughs, advanced users get condensed task lists and shortcuts.

Suggested top-level IA (labels are placeholders):
- Observe (dashboards, traces, alert timeline, model-quality monitors)
- Operate (routes, traffic policies, autoscaling controls, fallback policies)
- Deploy (model catalog, rollouts, canaries, version pins)
- Cost (token breakdown, per-route cost estimates, batch tuning suggestions)
- Debug (logs, debug bundle, reruns, presubmitted evals)
- Admin (teams, quotas, keys) - minimize prominence for day-to-day workflows

Wireframe notes / behavior rules (quick, hand-sketch descriptions):
- Left column: compact collapsed rail (icons + 1-line labels on hover) by default for desktop. Rail width must be consistent across pages to avoid layout jump.
- Top quick-action bar: appears under global header when a route or model is selected; shows 3 task actions (e.g., "Run canary", "Open trace", "Estimate cost") + keyboard hints (Cmd/Ctrl+K to focus, then 1/2/3).
- Breadcrumb + context header: route/model card at top of page with small metadata chips (region, model variant, last deploy, SLO status). Clicking the chip filters page content.
- Page subnav: when inside a task domain, subnav tabs align left with importance-ordered items; secondary tools live in an overflow.
- Empty / degraded states: provide succinct recovery steps and a one-click toggle to switch to a cached summary or to a fallback model.

Routing and fallback matrix (high level):
- Primary route: API-driven live view (fastest, full features).
- Fallback A: cached-summary (last successful snapshot, readonly).
- Fallback B: reduced mode (metrics-only, no interactive charts).
- Fallback C: service-unavailable banner + suggested next steps (open ticket, rerun check).
Notes: map these fallbacks to feature flags so Dedicated/private customers can opt-in or out.

Keyboard-first flow assumptions:
- Global focus (Cmd/Ctrl+K) opens command palette. Palette offers verbs (Observe, Deploy, Cost) + entity completion (route/model).
- Quick-action numbers (1-3) should be stable per persona (user preference persisted).
- All interactive lists are navigable with arrow keys and enter; context menu available with ";" hotkey.

Edge cases & failure modes to validate in grooming:
- Deep-linking into nested views: must land users in a stable substate (preserve selected tab, highlight correct quick actions).
- Cached items stale across rollouts: surface timestamp prominently and allow forced refresh with a single click.
- Large orgs with many routes: provide a top-level route filter and saved views (personal + team-shared).
- Private deployment network partitions: ensure admin surfaces show degraded status and provide safe read-only analytics.

Backlog / groom items (priority ordered):
1) MVP: implement top-level IA change + persistent quick-action bar; wireframe + prototype A/B test with 50 users (sprint 1).
2) Keyboard palette baseline: Cmd/Ctrl+K + navigation verbs + entity autocomplete (sprint 1-2).
3) Fallback plumbing: API contract + UX patterns for cached-summary and reduced-mode (sprint 2).
4) Persona preference persistence: per-user quick-action mapping + saved views (sprint 2-3).
5) Onboarding flows: task tours for the Observe and Deploy surfaces (sprint 3).
6) Private/Dedicated feature flags: opt-outs for fallbacks and telemetry (coord with infra & sales, sprint 3).

Acceptance criteria (for MVP release):
- 80% of platform and ML engineer tasks reachable within 2 clicks from landing page in prototype test.
- Command palette returns first relevant result in top 3 items for 90% of sampled queries.
- Degraded-mode renders within 400ms using cached-summary endpoint when primary APIs time out.

Open questions / decisions needed from design & infra:
- Should "Cost" be top-level or nested under "Observe"? (ask product analytics: combined queries per session).
- How many quick-actions are optimal on mobile? (propose 2 instead of 3).
- SLA for cached-summary freshness per tenant tier (free vs. enterprise).

Next steps:
- Team: product-console + eng-platform sync to finalize API for cached-summary (Diego to own).
- Design: produce hi-fi frames for top-level IA + microinteractions for quick-action bar (Janelle).
- Research: run 8 moderated task sessions on prototype and collect time-to-task metrics (Samir).
- Engineering: spike the Command Palette and persist user preferences (PR reference above).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally persona-first; expect some overlap with previous entity-first drafts. The goal is to validate whether task-aligned navigation measurably reduces context switching for our top personas. Look for potential risks to enterprise mental models (teams/keys) and suggest alternative placement if needed.

Appendix (sketch hints):
- Quick-action bar mock: icon, label, hotkey badge, dropdown for extra actions.
- Cached-summary card: timestamp, short list of key metrics (p50, p95, token rate), "refresh" and "open live" controls.
- Route list view: compact rows with pill filters (region, model, status) and an inline "run canary" button per row.

-- end of draft --
